meta.title: Krizaka UI — the open-source design system of Krizaka
meta.description: Krizaka UI: React and React Native components, tokens, icons, fonts, charts and page templates — documented from their code, accessible, in dark and light. An open-source project by Krizaka, Montréal.
meta.ogAlt: Krizaka UI — components, tokens, icons and templates, web and React Native

ui.title: Krizaka UI
ui.description: Tokens, Tailwind preset and React primitives — live previews, copyable code, props.

screens.intro: A screen is a layout's example that is a whole screen of a product: real words, the blocks it is made of, its phone version thought out. Copy it into the product, keep its structure, change the words.
screens.phone: On a phone, resize the frame or open the layout's page: every template reads in one column.

statusLong.stable: Stable: its API only changes in a major version.
statusLong.beta: Beta: its API may still change in a minor version.
statusLong.experimental: Experimental: created for a filed need, it may change or go in any minor version, until its first app uses it.
statusLong.deprecated: Deprecated: kept for the apps that still use it, removed in its next major.

component.nativeSetup: Wrap the app once in ThemeProvider from @krizaka/ui/native: every component reads its colour roles.
component.nativeCode: React Native has no live preview on the web: each example shows the screenshot of its story, tested in both themes, and the code to copy.

index.title: Krizaka UI
index.description: The design system every Krizaka product is built on — tokens, a Tailwind preset and accessible React primitives.

tokens.title: Colours & tokens
tokens.description: The --kz-* vocabulary: colours, surfaces, radii, shadows — one set of semantic roles compiled to CSS, TypeScript and React Native.

tailwind.title: Tailwind preset
tailwind.description: The Tailwind CSS v4 preset that turns the --kz-* tokens into utilities.

intl.title: Intl
intl.description: Money, numbers, dates and plurals formatted the same way in every Krizaka product.

query.title: Query
query.description: Server state for every Krizaka app: TanStack Query behind one package — typed fetch, Problem Details errors, live invalidation, App Router hydration, an offline cache on Expo.

typography.title: Typography
typography.description: Young Serif names, Atkinson Hyperlegible Next reads, Courier Prime types the notes: the Krizaka faces, their scale and their rules — self-hosted, web and mobile.

icons.title: Icons
icons.description: The Krizaka signature icons: cut corners, a node at the core — search, copy, and the rules of use.

installation.title: Installation
installation.description: Install Krizaka UI in a Next.js or Expo app: the packages, the stylesheet, the first component.

theming.title: Theming a product
theming.description: How a product wears Krizaka UI: brand scopes, dark and light, and the values a theme may change.

motion.title: Motion
motion.description: One motion system: easing, durations, the arrival of blocks and the rule that stills it all under reduced motion.

navigation.title: Navigation in the family
navigation.description: One top bar for every Krizaka site and product: what is shared, what each product makes its own, the language switch, the check.

layouts.title: Frames, layouts and templates
layouts.description: Which frame, layout or template to start from, on the web, on a phone and in a Mac window, and at which size class.

cahier-site.title: Cahier site
cahier-site.description: How a tool site wears krizaka.com's identity: the Cahier, its own bird and hue, taped prints, doodles and grades — one language, never one layout.

shop-presets.title: Shop presets
shop-presets.description: The twelve looks of a shop page, two per trade: accent, paper, faces and photo treatment as data, each proven accessible in both themes.

brand-marks.title: Brand marks
brand-marks.description: The four marks of the Krizaka family — drawn in code, animated, still under reduced motion.

i18n.title: i18n
i18n.description: Typed messages, formatting and rich text for every Krizaka app, with the CLI that checks both languages.

realtime.title: Realtime
realtime.description: The server bus and presence behind live screens: memory, PostgreSQL or Redis, delivered over SSE.

push.title: Push
push.description: Mobile notifications through the Expo Push Service: batching, receipts and dead tokens, with no dependency.

discovery.title: Discovery
discovery.description: Service discovery for the mobile apps: a signed manifest of backend addresses, a host allow-list and a fallback order, so a URL change never forces a store republish.

app-client.title: App client
app-client.description: What every Expo app shares: the bearer session over a storage port, the discovery client with a product's address, and the API client (bearer, timeout, 401 handling).

app-desktop.title: App desktop
app-desktop.description: What every Mac app calls on its native side, typed: folder grants and watches, the Keychain as the app client's storage, the native menu bar, deep links and the update channel.

app-config.title: App config
app-config.description: Version compatibility between apps and backends: minimum and latest version, soft and forced updates, maintenance, 426 Upgrade Required and N-1 contracts.

config.title: Config
config.description: The ESLint, TypeScript and Prettier presets, and the ratchet that counts the UI debt of an app.

platforms.title: Web · mobile · desktop
platforms.description: One design system on three platforms: where every component runs, why not elsewhere, and how to install each.

mobile.title: Parity with the web
mobile.description: What exists in React Native, and how each component differs from its web twin.

templates.title: All templates
templates.description: Whole pages and screens, grouped by what the person must do — each with the reason for its layout, live, with its phone version.

components.title: Components
components.description: Every component of Krizaka UI, by the job it does — web, React Native or both, with a live preview and filters.

typography.fallback: Until it loads: {fallback}, adjusted to its metrics (size-adjust {size}) — the text does not move.
typography.headline: Sovereign AI, on your own servers.
typography.paragraph: Your documents stay in Montréal. The answers cite their sources, the costs are counted in advance — 1 234,56 $ for 12 000 requests.

typography.webIntro: Import the faces once, next to the preset: the tokens already name them.
typography.nextIntro: Import the CSS in the root layout — the bundler copies and fingerprints the files; the fallbacks keep CLS at 0.
typography.nativeIntro: Load the static files with expo-font, then take a step of the scale and the name of its face.
typography.licenceIntro: Every face is under the SIL Open Font License 1.1: bundle it with any software, never sell it on its own. The licences ship in the package.
typography.registersLead: Krizaka's sites wear the Cahier; a product wears the calm register (ADR-006). The faces are the same package, set differently.
typography.registerSitesNote: Young Serif, one weight; Courier Prime for the notes; the pen (Krizaka Cahier) in the margin.
typography.registerProductNote: Plus Jakarta Sans at 550–700 for titles; Courier Prime for identifiers and times; the system monospace for code; never the pen.

get-started.title: Get started
get-started.when: You come here to install Krizaka UI, wear a product's theme and see a first screen working.

foundations.title: Foundations
foundations.when: You come here for the raw material: colours and tokens, type, icons, motion and the brand marks.

components.title: Components
components.when: You come here to find the piece that does a job — a button, a field, a dialog, a chart — grouped by what it does.

patterns.title: Patterns
patterns.when: You come here when one component is not enough: the blocks a page is made of and the layouts of whole screens.

templates.title: Templates
templates.when: You come here to start a whole page, grouped by what the person must do: be convinced, understand, see, act, work, talk, recover.

tooling.title: Tooling
tooling.when: You come here for the packages without pixels: the Tailwind preset, formatting, messages, server state, realtime, push and lint rules.

platforms.title: Platforms
platforms.when: You come here to know where a component runs — web, mobile, the desktop app — why it does not run elsewhere, and how to install each platform.

actions.title: Actions
actions.when: You come here to let someone do something: a button, a confirmation, a floating action.

inputs.title: Inputs & forms
inputs.when: You come here to collect something: a field, a choice, a date, a whole form.

navigation.title: Navigation
navigation.when: You come here to move around: bars, tabs, steps, a command palette.

overlays.title: Overlays
overlays.when: You come here to put something over the page: dialogs, menus, popovers, tooltips, sheets.

feedback.title: Feedback
feedback.when: You come here to say what is happening: alerts, loaders, toasts, empty states, progress.

data.title: Data
data.when: You come here to show information: tables, lists, cards, figures, profiles, chat.

media.title: Media
media.when: You come here to play, capture or edit images, video and sound.

maps.title: Maps
maps.when: You come here to show where things are, with open-source maps that cost nothing per view.

charts.title: Charts
charts.when: You come here to draw numbers: lines, bars, gauges, funnels — accessible, with their table.

brand.title: Brand & mascots
brand.when: You come here to make a page feel like Krizaka: the birds, the signature visuals and effects.

utilities.title: Utilities
utilities.when: You come here for the small tools every component is built on: class merging, slots, theming, text, dividers.

blocks.title: Page blocks
blocks.when: The pieces a page is made of: hero, sections, cards that argue, calls to act.

layouts.title: Screen layouts
layouts.when: The shells of whole screens: an app, a dashboard, settings, sign-in, an object and its list.

convince.title: Convince
convince.when: You come here when a visitor must decide: a landing, a product, a price, a comparison, a proof.

explain.title: Explain
explain.when: You come here when a reader must understand: how it works, a documentation hub or article, a changelog, a FAQ, a policy.

show.title: Show
show.when: You come here when the work itself is the argument: a gallery, a story, a case study, an object and its details.

act.title: Act
act.when: You come here when a person must do something once: reach the team, sign in or up, set up, pay.

operate.title: Operate
operate.when: You come here when a person works every day: a dashboard, a console with a table, settings, an app shell.

converse.title: Converse
converse.when: You come here when people talk: an inbox, a chat, comments, a notifications centre.

recover.title: Recover
recover.when: You come here when the way is blocked: an empty list, an error, a missing page, maintenance, a product still being built.

mobile.intro: What runs in React Native, from @krizaka/ui/native. Most components exist on both platforms with the same name and the same props; a few exist only on mobile, because the platform asks for them (a tab bar, a sheet, a pull to refresh).

wall.title: On a phone
wall.lead: {count} React Native stories at a phone's width — whole screens first, then the richest story of each component. Each one is the screenshot of its story, retaken when the code changes; open a component for its code.

brand.intro: The four marks of the Krizaka family, from @krizaka/ui. Each is drawn in code (no image to ship), animated when the page allows it, and still under reduced motion. A change to a mark is made in krizaka-ui, released, then adopted.
brand.use: Use the mark where the product is named: the header, the sign-in, the loader and the splash — never a copy, never a placeholder.
brand.manifest: All the files and their checksums (manifest.json)
brand.note: Generated from the code of @krizaka/ui by tools/export-brand.mjs — never hand-made. Logos and marks, dark and light, PNG 256/512/1024, avatars 500/1024, social previews 1280×640.

flock.title: The flock
flock.intro: The birds of Krizaka carry its promises — each one has a loop, rendered from the code of @krizaka/ui (the same Mascot the products use), dark and light, still under reduced motion.
flock.source: The loops are rendered by tools/brand-films: the real components, filmed frame by frame in a headless browser. When a mark or a bird changes, they are rendered again.

promises.owl: reads every page, knows every face

platforms.intro: Krizaka UI is one design system on three platforms: the web (React), mobile (React Native and Expo) and the desktop (the Orazaka Mac app, whose Tauri window renders the web components). Every component says where it runs and, where it does not, why — a gap to build, tracked by an issue, or a platform it is not meant for, with what to use there.
platforms.count: {yes} components · {gap} to build · {na} not meant for it

web.title: Web
web.what: React 19 and Tailwind CSS v4: one entry per component, server-rendered by default, every token a CSS variable.

native.title: Mobile
native.what: React Native and Expo: the same names and props from @krizaka/ui/native, on the same tokens, dark and light, with roles and labels for screen readers.
native.use: Then, at the root of your app

desktop.title: Desktop
desktop.what: The Orazaka Mac app is a Tauri 2 window: the web components run there as they are, and a few have a desktop form — the app shell's title bar, density and menu keys (ADR-002).

platforms.matrixLead: Every component of @krizaka/ui and @krizaka/charts, read from the parity its meta declares. A new web component without a mobile and a desktop decision does not build.
platforms.legend: ✓ runs there · ✗ to build (its issue) · n/a not meant for it (what to use). For how each mobile component differs from its web twin:
